b: There are plenty of creatures to spot along Dublin's River Dodder, but few walkers expect to encounter a rhinoceros. Standing on a plinth in the middle of the river near Classon's Bridge is a remarkably lifelike, life-size bronze rhino that has become one of Milltown's strangest landmarks.

The animal appeared seemingly overnight in 2002, with no plaque explaining who created it, who put it there, or why a rhinoceros was chosen. Contemporary reports noted that nobody had claimed responsibility, and the nearby Dropping Well pub denied being behind its mysterious arrival. The pub nevertheless embraced its unusual neighbour, even running a competition to give the creature a name. Suggestions included “Rhino O'Neal,” “The Plodder in the Dodder,” and “The Milltown Muddler.”

The Dodder itself soon added to the mystery. During flooding in November 2002, the rhino disappeared beneath the swollen river, leaving Dubliners waiting for the water to fall to discover whether their new resident had survived. It did, and more than two decades later the bronze beast is still standing watch over the Dodder.

Today, spotting the rhino is one of the more surreal surprises on a walk along the river. Its creator and the full story of how it arrived remain uncertain, leaving Dublin with a piece of public art whose mystery is almost as memorable as the sculpture itself.
